emma_support: Hey team — ACME (customer) opened an escalated ticket. Their Private VPC traffic is egressing through a NAT/peer that routes to eu-west, causing ~250ms cross-region latency and occasional 403s because the token region doesn't match. They see X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1 on requests from our logs but they're in us-east-1. Can someone triage?

acme_ops: Confirming. Started seeing spike ~09:10 UTC. App in us-east-1. When we hit api.redwood.internal we get ~200ms+ and some 403s json: {"error":"region_mismatch"}. We believe our NAT/peering changed after a routing update.

emma_support: Thanks, added SRE and networking. Can you share a sample curl and the source public IP?

acme_ops: Here's minimal repro:

curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" https://api.redwood.internal/v1/generate?model=redwood-1

Response headers include:
X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1
X-Request-Id: r-9c4d

Public IP: 34.210.44.66 (elastic NAT on our side)

acme_ops: attaching traceroute and a short tcpdump.

acme_ops: traceroute to api.redwood.internal resolves to 52.15.20.1 then jumps to eu-gw transit 185.72.33.1 -> 18.194.x.x (eu LB)

acme_ops: tcpdump shows SNAT to 34.210.44.66 then traffic to transit-gw -> peering -> eu edge

derek_sre: Got it. Likely transit/VPC peering egress path is preferring a eu Transit Gateway attachment. Two initial asks: 1) can you share route table for the private subnet + nat gw route? 2) VPC Flow Logs for a sample window (09:05-09:15 UTC) so we can see next-hop/ASN.

maria_network: Looping in network — @derek_sre what I suspect: customer has a shared Transit Gateway with multiple attachments (us-east and eu-west) and the route table for the TG attachment has a more specific CIDR route pointing to the eu attachment, so SNAT'ed traffic ends up egressing eu. Also possible: partner-proxy/transparent HTTP proxy in front of egress rewriting Host/headers.

acme_ops: Sharing route table & flow logs in a sec. We also have a managed partner VPN; not sure if that hops through a partner colo.

deploy-bot: deploy #service-ingress 2026-01-12T09:02:17 succeeded (canary -> stable)

maria_network: If the SNAT EIP belongs to the customer's NAT in us-east but the transit GW path prefers eu, that still can route to eu for physical egress. Need to confirm which internet egress ASN we hit.

derek_sre: On Redwood side I pulled the request logs for r-9c4d. It shows incoming source IP 34.210.44.66 and we marked it routed to eu-west LB at 18.194.x.x. We have a fallback policy that picks the nearest healthy region by source IP geo / peering mapping; but since source IP is registered in a block that peers through eu transit, our geo lookup maps it to eu.

emma_support: So root cause likely customer's egress -> transit mapping causes source IP to be associated with eu. Two parallel tracks: 
1) customer/networking: fix NAT/Transit route so egress exits us-east (preferred).
2) Redwood product mitigation: we can accept region_hint header to pin region to us-east-1 for a short period to reduce impact and avoid fallback routing.

acme_ops: Region-hinting would be helpful while we fix routing. How do we set that?

derek_sre: You can add header X-Redwood-Region: us-east-1 on requests or pass ?region=us-east-1 param. I'll verify ACLs — some tokens might be region-locked which caused the 403s. If token is issued for us-east, requests landing in eu will 403 with region_mismatch.

maria_network: For customers using TGW or partner VPN, watch out for asymmetric routing. If return path goes different region, egress decisions can be off. Recommend checking:
- TGW route tables for prefix priorities
- NAT gateway SNAT EIP ownership and advertised route path (BGP)
- Partner colo/config for hairpinning proxies
- Any transparent HTTP proxies (squid/varnish) that rewrite headers

acme_ops: We found a route in the TGW route table that points 0.0.0.0/0 to the eu attachment for that attachment's route priority — looks like an automation accidentally modified the attachment routes. Rolling back now.

acme_ops: Quick test after rollback: traceroute now goes to us-east egress 3 hops earlier. curl response headers show X-Redwood-Region: us-east-1 and latency down to 22ms. No 403s for 10 test requests.

acme_ops: Sharing post-rollback flow logs and the IaC change that caused it.

derek_sre: Great. We'll monitor for 1 hour and confirm no further misrouted traffic. We'll also patch our region resolution to prefer customer-configured IP -> region mappings when present (we have an internal mapping override feature, filing a ticket).

maria_network: Quick notes for docs: customers with TGW attachments spanning regions should ensure the egress route is explicit per attachment. Avoid wide 0.0.0.0/0 pointing to a multi-region attachment unless you intend eu egress.

sophia_account: ACME — glad this was reversible quickly. I'll keep them updated and offer a follow-up call to review TGW best practices.

emma_support: Action items: 
- acme_ops: confirm no regressions and share final flow logs (ACME) [open]
- derek_sre: add internal ticket to support region override mapping and document X-Redwood-Region header behavior [open]
- maria_network: create short KB for TGW egress pitfalls and add to support docs [open]
- sophia_account: schedule customer review [open]

logs-bot: NOTE: 1765123456 thread marked high-priority; linked ticket S-23421

acme_ops: thanks everyone — will ping if any oddities. :tada:

emma_support: closing notes in ticket after 60m of stable checks. Thanks all :raised_hands:
